minutes.headline: Board deferred two solar contracts and opened the Special Town Meeting warrant for November 28.
minutes.summary: The board heard a facilities director's briefing on risks in two solar contracts and agreed to take no action, leaving a possible special meeting. It heard a Summer Street project update and public comment on ballot Question 2. It deferred the Mart van agreement for more information, opened the special town meeting warrant, and planned town manager finalist interviews.

what_happened.line: The Select Board opened the warrant for a Special Town Meeting on November 28, with the warrant closing October 25.
The board deferred the Mart van agreement until it has information on refused calls and workers comp and input from the finance committee; the motion was withdrawn.
After a briefing on risks in two solar contracts, the board took no action, with a special meeting likely if materials are ready.
The board voted to declare high school rooftop space surplus and send a letter to the commissioner.
The board directed that a legal counsel RFP be issued soon, with about 45 days to respond.

why_it_matters: The solar contracts and the Mart van agreement both carry long-term costs the town budget, mostly taxes, would pick up, and the Special Town Meeting is where residents may be asked to vote on related spending.
Rooftop space, the Summer Street project cost and a possible back-tax bill on the 61B property all bear on what the town pays or earns in future years.
watch_next: The Special Town Meeting on November 28, with the warrant closing October 25.
The legal counsel RFP, due to be issued soon with about 45 days to respond, and a possible special board meeting on the solar contracts.
